0: Opening pose: the carrier comes nearly bow on; the doodle's slab seen from just off its bow (6 degrees), deck foreshortened, the near long edge and the underside line leaning back to the left, the bow edge across the deck's front edge.
6: Same heading while the camera pans; the slab slides right with the deck's front edge.
12: Still nearly bow on; the slab rides a little lower as the ship approaches.
18: The ship approaches; the slab grows slightly, heading barely changed.
24: Last moment of the near-still approach: the slab has only crept round a degree or two.
27: The swing begins: the slab rotates a little faster, the near long edge leaning further over.
30: Swing under way; the near side of the slab starts to widen.
33: The port deck edge lengthens; the bow face still square to the camera.
36: The port side of the deck reads as a short diagonal from the island down to the front-left corner.
39: The swing speeds up: the port deck edge leans further over and the side of the hull begins to show under it.
40: Breakdown in the fast part of the swing: keeps the port edge lengthening evenly frame to frame.
41: Breakdown: the bow face starts to slide right under the deck edge.
42: Breakdown into the line: the port deck edge runs from the island to the bow corner and the hull side opens below it.
43: Breakdown after 42: the hull side under the port deck edge widens.
44: Breakdown into the line: the deck diagonal steepens toward its three-quarter angle.
45: The line: the bow has swung off the camera, the deck reads as a long diagonal from the island to the bow with the port hull side showing under it.
46: Breakdown after the line: the swing keeps going, the stern end slides off the left of the frame.
47: Breakdown: the bow face narrows as it turns away to the right.
48: Follow-through: the swing carries on and the ship grows as it closes on the camera.
49: Last frame: three-quarter view, the deck diagonal from upper left to the bow corner, the bow face turned to the right.
